entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Epiphanius of Pavia (438–496), later venerated as Saint Epiphanius of Pavia, was Bishop of Pavia from 466 until his death in 496. Epiphanius additionally held the offices of lector, subdeacon and deacon.

As Bishop of Pavia, Epiphanius played a key role in shaping the Christian Church in 5th-century Italy. He was a strong advocate for the use of the Latin language in liturgical services and worked to establish the office of the bishop as a central institution in the Church. This move had significant consequences for the development of Christianity in the Western Roman Empire.

Epiphanius' legacy extends beyond his own time, influencing the development of Christianity in the Middle Ages and shaping the course of European religious history. He was an important figure in the struggle for religious authority between the Catholic Church and the Western Roman Empire.

The legacy of Epiphanius of Pavia can still be seen in the enduring importance of the office of the bishop in Christian tradition. His emphasis on the use of Latin in liturgical services also contributed to the development of a distinctively Western Christian culture.

 Epiphanius of Pavia was born in the late 4th century in what is now modern-day Italy, but the exact date of his birth is unknown. He was educated in Rome and later became a deacon before being appointed Bishop of Pavia in 466. He played a significant role in the development of the Christian Church in Italy during the 5th century.
